meta.title: SŌN — Fusuma Art from Japan
meta.description: SŌN brings fusuma — Japanese sliding panels of paper and wood — to spaces around the world, as art that changes a room. Join the waitlist.

hero.title: Paper that holds the light.
hero.lead: SŌN brings fusuma — Japanese sliding panels of paper and wood — to homes, studios and hotels around the world, as art that changes a room.
hero.visualAlt: Illustration of two fusuma panels sliding open to let soft light through.

letters.body: The tradition of Japan, the care of the artisans, and the soul we put into every piece.
A culture born in Japan, and a return to the origin of fusuma art.
Not only preserving tradition, but carrying it forward as a new form of art.

about.title: A wall that moves. A surface that glows.
about.body: Fusuma are Japanese sliding panels made of layers of paper on a light wooden frame. For centuries they have shaped how light and space move through a Japanese home — closing to create a quiet room, opening to join two spaces into one.

points.title: Light & shadow
points.body: Washi paper softens the light. The day moves across its surface, and shadow becomes part of the room.

points.title: Transition
points.body: Slide it open, and two rooms become one. Slide it closed, and a quiet place appears.

points.title: A canvas
points.body: The surface of a fusuma has long been a canvas — for paper, pattern and painting.

craft.title: Made by many hands
craft.lead: A fusuma brings several crafts together in one panel.

steps.title: Frame
steps.body: A light wooden lattice forms the core of the panel.

steps.title: Layers
steps.body: Layers of paper are pasted onto the lattice by a paper-mounting artisan, or hyōgu-shi.

steps.title: Surface
steps.body: The final washi — or an artwork — is applied as the face of the panel.

steps.title: Edge & pull
steps.body: A wooden edge frames the panel, and the hikite, the recessed pull, is set in place.

craft.note: We are working with artisans in Japan. Their names and stories will be shared here with their permission.
